answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The opal multiplier is published, charged in delta, and pearl lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2628 identities would post 3161 proofs and burn roughly 90 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
